target_customer: Developers and teams deploying Docker projects to Kubernetes clusters
problem: Moving a Docker project from development to a Kubernetes cluster was complex. Redspread's open-source Spread tool deployed with a single command and versioned environments, described as Git for Kubernetes.
business_model: Open-source developer tool with planned commercial deployment product; revenue not found

founders.name: Mackenzie Burnett
founders.background_notes: YC bio: background in open source software infrastructure, climate security and international policy.

founders.name: Dan Gillespie
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A CLI bridging Docker builds and Kubernetes objects required Kubernetes expertise while the project was still young; standard engineering with hard integration parts.

defensibility.rationale: An open-source tool in an area the Kubernetes project and vendors could absorb quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CoreOS acquired the team in October 2016 to fold the technology into Tectonic and push it upstream to Kubernetes.

market_need_then: Kubernetes adoption was growing in 2016 and deploying to it was a common complaint; no direct demand metrics for Redspread were found.

branding.domain_note: redspread.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page.

identity.logo: A simple single-shape mark per an automated logo catalog (unverified)
identity.voice_and_tone: CoreOS CEO quoted calling Spread like Git for Kubernetes

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand press beyond acquisition coverage; the open-source project name Spread was confusable with other Spread projects.

outcome_analysis: Redspread built an open-source Kubernetes deployment tool in the Winter 2016 batch and was acquired by CoreOS on October 17, 2016, about seven months after the batch. Terms were undisclosed and VentureBeat called it not a major financial deal. The founders joined CoreOS and the technology was slated for Tectonic and upstream Kubernetes, which makes it a team and technology absorption rather than a standalone product outcome.
notes: No funding round found. Crunchbase total $240K (via TechCrunch snippet) and CB Insights $120K conflict, both unverified aggregator figures. The eWeek and Register acquisition coverage appeared in search results and the VentureBeat article was opened. Competitor search returned only undated StackShare pages, and the only dated source (VentureBeat, 2016-10-17) is after the batch, so the list is empty. That piece named Google Cloud, AWS, Docker and Mesosphere as container players. Rounds exist per CB Insights (120K over 2 rounds, CoreOS as investor) and Crunchbase via TechCrunch snippet (240K total) but no round dates or amounts were opened, so none recorded.
